thread:
maria: Heads-up — saw a hard OOM on dedicated-prod during a long-context smoke run (50k tokens).

maria: Process killed: inference_runtime PID=4219, OOM killer invoked.

maria: paste of dmesg snippet:
```
[1755123456.123456] Out of memory: Killed process 4219 (inference_runtime) total-vm:12000000kB, anon-rss:4800000kB, file-rss:0kB, shmem-rss:0kB
[1755123456.123789] oom_reaper: reaped process 4219 (inference_runtime)
```

sam: ugh. which KV config were we running? slab_size/evict policy?

maria: default slab=1GB, reuse_threshold=0.25, eviction=LIFO (recent-first). No compacting in this build.

liam: Did we see fragmentation or steady growth? any per-slab hist?

maria: profiler shows steady growth of "kv_total_alloc" across sequences (attached short dump) — memory doesn't drop on context switch. Looks like KV pages pinned by huge-key reuse that prevents eviction.

ana: can we force compaction of cold slabs during long contexts? We discussed slab rotation earlier.

sam: two short mitigations: 1) on soft-oom, immediately disable KV caching for that session and retry; 2) proactively evict oldest 30% of slabs when per-session memory > 70% of slab cap. both low-risk.

liam: we also had a kernel-selection nuance: some attention kernels allocate temporary scratch on device which pushes device mem closer to host pinned KV; combined load triages badly. maybe route long-contexts to more conservative kernels that avoid large temp buffers.

maria: good call. for now I can push a hotfix to: 
- detect sustained kv_total_alloc growth > 5%/min for 3 mins -> mark session as "kv-heavy"
- on next request, return header X-Runtime-Fallback: kv-disabled and fall back to streaming generation without cache
- increment metric kv_fallback_count

ops-bot: deploy queued: infra/kv-hotfix -> staging (canary 2 hosts)

sam: can we also add a graceful fallback that retries the same request against a smaller context window (truncate earliest tokens) before disabling KV completely? that preserves continuity for chat apps.

maria: yes — plan: try truncation -> if still approaching threshold, disable KV and retry. will tag rollback criteria.

liam: long-term: implement slab compaction + fuzzy-reuse map so repeated token sequences reuse same KV entries instead of allocating new pages. Also think about a background GC sweep that reclaims unreachable fragments after N seconds idle.

ana: need tests. create a stress harness that simulates 50k token streams with repeated but slightly mutated prefixes to exercise fragmentation. add as part of nightly perf.

maria: i'll open PR with hotfix + tests. will also add dashboards: kv_total_alloc, kv_frag_ratio, kv_fallback_count, kernel_temp_alloc.

sam: add runbook snippet to incidents/soft-ooms: recommended immediate action: toggle kv-disabled per-session, escalate if >3 host OOMs in 1h.

maria: tracking: ENG-RT-482 (hotfix), ENG-RT-483 (stress harness), ENG-RT-484 (slab compaction design).

liam: thumbs up. after hotfix canary -> 24h soak, then roll to dedicated fleet. :thumbsup:

maria: waving flag if anyone wants to pair on the PR review tomorrow morning.

ana: I'll take review.

sam: thanks all. keeping an eye on metrics.
